Hi Alex — great to hear, and congrats on moving to a dedicated plan.

I've attached our pre-sales sizing worksheet and a short checklist of the telemetry fields that give us the fastest route to a defensible capacity estimate. The minimal set we need is:
- per-minute QPS (or timestamped request log)
- prompt token length distribution (percentiles)
- generation token length distribution (percentiles)
- session/session_id mapping or session timeout heuristic
- top-10 API routes (if you have multiple prompt shapes)

If you can share a 48–72 hour sample in CSV or NDJSON with timestamps and route labels, we'll run a quick pass and return a pilot sizing sketch (nodes / GPU mix / expected QPS and cost envelope).

I looped in Marissa (capacity lead) and Karthik (pre-sales infra) to help with the technical assumptions and to set up a follow-up call. Proposed slots: Wed 3pm PT or Thu 11am PT — do either work?

Attachments: redwood_pre-sales_sizing_worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), telemetry_checklist.txt

Best,

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: quick notes for Skyline worksheet (prelim assumptions)

Vanessa / Karthik — posting a short internal note before the call so we're aligned. Key unknowns from Alex's note: model family, quantization target, and sessionization behavior. My baseline assumptions below for the sketch:
- Model: assume an open-chat 7B (we can revise if they have 13B/70B).
- Quantization: assume int8-recipe -> ~2x GPU throughput improvement vs float16. Mark as tunable.
- Latency SLO: ask if p99 target is <= 500ms; we'll size for p99=400ms as conservative.
- Prompt/generation mix: assume 1:2 prompt to generation token ratio for pilot if they don't provide exacts.
- Session affinity: assume sticky sessions for multi-turn KV cache; this increases memory needs per slot.

Prelim capacity sketch (very rough): pilot cluster for 30 QPS sustained / 120 QPS peak burst -> 4 x A100-80GB equiv nodes (shared with autoscale/burst) OR 8 x H100-80GB for lower latency per-node. We'll refine after telemetry.

Questions to confirm on the call:
1) Are you able to provide a 72-hour sample with per-request token counts and a session_id?
2) Do you run temperature/top-k sweeps in production or is generation deterministic?
3) Any regulatory requirements for VPC/on-prem that would change deployment model?

I'll prepare a short workbook with cost envelopes and a candidate GPU mix. Vanessa, want me to own the sizing sketch for the pilot deliverable?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Capacity Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Alex Rivera <alex@skyline.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+infra@skyline.ai
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning - Skyline conversational product

Hi Vanessa / Marissa — thanks for the checklist, and apologies for the delay. Attached is a 72-hour extract (sanitized) that matches your fields. Answers inline below.

Answers to your questions:
1) Attached CSV includes timestamp, session_id, route, prompt_tokens, gen_tokens, backend_model_tag.
2) Model: we're currently on oss-7b-chat for production pilot; we may trial a 13B variant late Q3.
3) Quantization: plan is bfloat16 in production, but we can experiment with int8 for cost review.
4) Latency SLO: primary product requires p95 < 250ms and p99 < 600ms for UI interactions; background workers tolerate higher. For the pilot, we want to target p95 = 220ms, p99 = 500ms (user experience focused).
5) Traffic shape: average QPS = 28, sustained daytime 18–35, peak bursts up to 125 QPS (10–12 minute spikes), average concurrent sessions observed ~42, peak concurrent sessions ~130. Median session length 3.2 minutes; top quartile ~9 minutes (multi-turn).
6) Prompt/generation sizes: median prompt 120 tokens, median generation 260 tokens. 90th pct prompt = 430 tokens; 90th pct gen = 780 tokens.
7) Routes: 70% of traffic uses a short Q&A route (prompt ~40 tokens), 20% a multi-turn assistant (longer prompts & gen), 10% batch/analytics (non-latency sensitive).
8) Security: we need VPC peering and SOC2 evidence (we can share on request).

Attached: skyline_sample_telemetry.csv (72h extract)

Next steps: happy to take the pilot sizing sketch and schedule Wed 3pm PT to review (that slot works for our infra team).

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Product
Skyline AI
